findings.body:
**`cmd_measure` sorts items it never measured (crq.py:2561).**

Line 2557 skips followup merged items that have state `skipped` and no `measure`. The skipped item still stays in `merged`. The sort key at crq.py:2561 then reads `i["measure"]["docs_only"]` for every item in `merged`. Any skipped followup item without a measure raises `KeyError`. The command then crashes before `save_queue(q)` and `write_status(q)`, so `crq measure` cannot finish while such an item exists. The print loop at crq.py:2568-2569 reads `i["measure"]` in the same way.

Rank only the items that were measured.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    for i in merged:
+    measured = []
+    for i in merged:
         if i.get("source") == "followup" and i["state"] == "skipped" and not i.get("measure"):
             continue  # merged head already reviewed; not a supersession decision
         apply_measure(i)
+        measured.append(i)
     # rank: code before docs-only, then most surviving non-doc lines first
-    ranked = sorted(merged, key=lambda i: (i["measure"]["docs_only"], -i["measure"]["surviving_nondoc"],
+    ranked = sorted(measured, key=lambda i: (i["measure"]["docs_only"], -i["measure"]["surviving_nondoc"],
                                            -i["measure"]["surviving"]))
```
</details>
findings.title: `cmdmeasure` sorts items it never measured (crq.py:2561).

findings.body:
**Catch `repair_tick.enqueue` failures on the completed-cycle path so one failure does not stop the tick.**

`harvest_review` calls `repair_tick.enqueue` at `crq.py:1815` with no exception handler. The merged-current receipt path at `crq.py:1739-1741` wraps the same call, so the cycle path lacks that guard.

If `enqueue` raises here, the exception leaves `harvest_review` and the per-item loop in `tick()` at `crq.py:2382-2386`. The same tick then skips `repair_tick.harvest`, `repair_tick.backfill`, and `repair_tick.reconcile_fix_prs` at `crq.py:2391-2401`. The last save before the loop is at `crq.py:2371`, so the persisted item can still show `state == "reviewing"` with its `run` set. The next tick repeats the harvest. A deterministic `enqueue` failure stops every tick at this item. A transient failure clears on a later tick.

A handler that sets the item to `"done"` does not recover the repair debt. `repair_tick.backfill` re-derives work from `item["cycles"]`, but it returns at `repair_tick.py:343-344` once `legacy_repair_backfilled` is set. That flag is set at `repair_tick.py:361-362`. After that, a skipped repair on a `done` item is not retried. The fix needs a retryable state that is not `done`, or a durable retry record, and that design should be settled before the handler changes.
findings.title: Catch `repairtick.enqueue` failures on the completed-cycle path so one failure does not stop the tick.

findings.body:
**`cmd_measure` can crash when sorting a skipped followup item that has no measure.**

The guard at `crq.py:2557` keeps a skipped followup item without `measure` in `merged`, and `apply_measure` never runs for it. The sort key at `crq.py:2561` then reads `i["measure"]["docs_only"]`, which raises `KeyError` for that item. The sort runs before `save_queue(q)` and `write_status(q)`, so `crq measure` cannot finish while such an item is in the queue.

The print loop does not add a separate failure. It iterates `ranked`, which is built by the same sort, so it runs only after the sort succeeds.

Rank only the items that were measured. Skipped followup items with no measure still persist and do not affect the ranking.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    for i in merged:
+    measured = []
+    for i in merged:
         if i.get("source") == "followup" and i["state"] == "skipped" and not i.get("measure"):
             continue  # merged head already reviewed; not a supersession decision
         apply_measure(i)
+        measured.append(i)
     # rank: code before docs-only, then most surviving non-doc lines first
-    ranked = sorted(merged, key=lambda i: (i["measure"]["docs_only"], -i["measure"]["surviving_nondoc"],
+    ranked = sorted(measured, key=lambda i: (i["measure"]["docs_only"], -i["measure"]["surviving_nondoc"],
                                            -i["measure"]["surviving"]))
```
</details>
